name: @gabrielpule/mcss-lite
description: Contract-first CSS design system: every class, state and token is declared in machine-readable contracts, so people and AI agents build UI with the right parts.
naming: BEM: block, block__element, block--modifier. State: data-state="value" on the block.

values.light: Light theme. Also the default when no data-theme attribute is set.
values.auto: Follows the operating system via prefers-color-scheme.

rules.title: Components never set their own outer margin
rules.text: Never add margin to a c-* root element. Put components inside a layout primitive (l-stack, l-cluster, l-grid, l-sidebar, l-switcher) and let it provide the spacing.

rules.title: Layout, then component, then utility, then token
rules.text: Solve a need with an l-* layout primitive first, then a c-* component and its modifiers, then a u-* utility. Only write custom CSS as a last resort, and then use var(--token) values only.

rules.title: Never invent class or token names
rules.text: Use only the classes, modifiers, elements, data-state values and tokens listed in this file. If something is missing, write custom CSS with existing tokens instead of guessing a name such as c-button--warning.

rules.title: States use data-state plus the native or ARIA pair
rules.text: Express component state with data-state="…" (for example data-state="error"), and always add the paired native attribute or ARIA listed for that state (disabled, aria-invalid, aria-busy).

rules.title: Theme with semantic tokens, never raw values
rules.text: Never hard-code colors (#hex, rgb()) or pixel spacing. Use semantic tokens (--color-text-default, --color-action-primary…) or component tokens (--button-primary-background…). Primitive color tokens (--color-gray-*, --color-blue-*) do not adapt to dark mode.

contentRules.title: Write in sentence case
contentRules.text: Capitalize only the first word and proper nouns in labels, titles, buttons and badges. Title Case is harder to scan and reads as shouting in long labels.

contentRules.title: Buttons say what happens
contentRules.text: Start with a verb and name the thing it acts on. A person should know the result before they click.

contentRules.title: No vague labels
contentRules.text: "Submit", "Click here", "Yes" and "More" say nothing out of context. Screen reader users often hear a list of every link or button on the page, with no surrounding text.

contentRules.title: Errors say what went wrong and how to fix it
contentRules.text: Name the problem in plain words and tell the person what to do. Don't blame, don't use codes, don't say "invalid".

contentRules.title: Show errors at the right moment
contentRules.text: Check a field when the person leaves it or submits the form, not while they type its first value. Once a field shows an error, clear it as soon as the value is fixed. After a failed submit, list every error at the top of the form, each linked to its field.
contentRules.do: There is a problem: Enter your email address
contentRules.dont: Email is invalid (shown after the first keystroke)

contentRules.title: Mark optional fields, not required ones
contentRules.text: Ask only for what you need, then add "(optional)" to the few fields people may skip. Rows of asterisks add noise and need a legend.

contentRules.title: Keep punctuation light
contentRules.text: No full stops on buttons, titles, labels or badges. Use full stops in help text and messages that are sentences. Avoid exclamation marks.

contentRules.title: Write numbers and dates the same way everywhere
contentRules.text: Use numerals for numbers, the full month name in dates and a consistent time format. Avoid ambiguous dates like 03/04.

contentRules.title: Write for everyone
contentRules.text: Use plain words, active voice and "you". Avoid idioms, jargon and gendered defaults. Describe what something does, not how it looks ("select", not "click the blue button").
contentRules.dont: Just hit the big blue button, guys

blocks.name: Badge
blocks.description: A short, non-interactive label for status or category, such as "Beta" or "Paid".

values.name: primary
values.description: Brand emphasis, e.g. "New".

values.name: success
values.description: Positive status, e.g. "Active".

values.name: warning
values.description: Needs attention, e.g. "Expiring".

values.name: error
values.description: Negative status, e.g. "Failed".

values.name: info
values.description: Neutral information, e.g. "Draft".

whenToUse: Showing the status of an item: Draft, Active, Failed.
A short category or plan label: Beta, Pro.
whenNotToUse: Anything clickable, removable or filterable: use `c-button` with c-button--sm.
A count on a navigation item: badges here are for status words, not numbers.
A sentence: use body text or an alert.
use: Keep badge text to one or two words.
avoid: Making a badge clickable; use c-button--sm instead.
Relying on badge color alone to convey meaning; the text must carry the status.

do.text: Say the status in words; the tone only supports it.
do.html: Failed Passed

dont.text: Don't make a badge clickable or invent tones.

content: One or two words, sentence case: "In review", not "IN REVIEW".
Each tone keeps one meaning across the product: error always means something failed.

a11y: Color is decorative; the badge text must describe the status on its own.

blocks.name: Button
blocks.description: Triggers an action. Apply to <button>. Apply to <a> only when the control navigates. Parts have a 2px keyline and a brick edge that drops when pressed.

values.name: primary
values.description: The main action in a view region. Use at most one per region.

values.name: secondary
values.description: Outlined in the action color; for important but not main actions.

values.name: ghost
values.description: No border or background; for low-emphasis actions such as Cancel.

values.name: danger
values.description: Destructive, hard-to-undo actions such as Delete. Brick red.

values.name: sm
values.description: Compact button for dense UI such as tables and toolbars.

values.name: lg
values.description: Large button for hero or empty-state calls to action.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The action cannot run right now. Rendered ghosted with a dashed keyline.
states.pair: Prefer aria-disabled="true": the button stays focusable, so link a visible reason with aria-describedby and ignore activation in your handler. The disabled attribute also works on <button> but removes it from the tab order. On <a>, set aria-disabled="true" and remove href.

states.name: loading
states.description: The action is in progress. Shows moving stripes; text keeps full contrast.
states.pair: Set aria-busy="true" and aria-disabled="true", keep the visible label (for example "Saving…"), and ignore activation in your handler.

whenToUse: The control does something on this page: submits a form, saves, deletes, opens a dialog, toggles a setting.
A confirming or cancelling action in a form or `c-modal` footer.
An on/off toolbar control such as Bold or Mute, with aria-pressed.
whenNotToUse: The control goes to another page or URL: use a plain link. Apply c-button to an <a> only when a link must look like a button, such as a start-page call to action.
Showing a status that does nothing when clicked: use `c-badge`.
Filtering or removing items in a list of tags: that is a chip, which MCSS-Lite does not ship yet.
use: Group buttons with l-cluster; it provides the gap.
Order a button group as secondary or ghost actions first, then the primary action last.
Write labels as verbs that name the outcome: "Save changes", not "OK".
For toggle buttons (for example a theme switch), set aria-pressed="true" on the selected one; it gets the pressed style automatically.
Use c-button--danger for the confirming action of anything destructive, never c-button--primary.
avoid: Adding margin to .c-button. Spacing belongs to the layout parent.
Combining two variant modifiers (for example c-button--primary c-button--ghost).

do.text: Use one primary button per region, placed last in its group.

dont.text: Don't combine two variants on one button to make it stand out more.

do.text: Keep an unavailable action focusable and say why it can't run, with aria-disabled and a linked reason.
do.html: Add a title before you publish.

dont.text: Don't grey out a button without saying why, or set the state without its native pair.

do.text: Invent nothing: a warning-style action is c-button--danger or a plain button.
do.html: <button type="button" class="c-button c-button--danger">Delete project</button>

dont.text: Don't guess a modifier that isn't in the contract.

content: Write a verb plus the thing it acts on: "Save changes", "Delete project". Never "OK", "Submit" or "Click here".
Use sentence case: "Create account", not "Create Account".
Keep the label the same when a toggle changes state; aria-pressed carries the state.
A danger button names what is destroyed: "Delete account", not "Confirm".
No full stop at the end of a label.

a11y: A button needs a visible text label, or aria-label when it only contains an icon.
Use type="button" unless the button submits a form.
c-button--sm looks compact but keeps a 44px tall hit area.
Don't disable a submit button until the form is valid. Let people submit, then show what is missing.

keyboard.action: Moves focus to the button, including one marked aria-disabled.

examples.html: Read the docs

sources.title: NN/g: Why disabled buttons hurt UX
Adrian Roselli: Be careful with dynamic accessible names

blocks.name: Card
blocks.description: A raised surface that groups related content, such as a summary, a settings group or a list item.

values.name: elevated

values.name: bordered

elements.name: header

elements.name: title

elements.name: footer

A dashboard summary that groups a figure with its actions.
A group of related settings.
whenNotToUse: People compare items side by side or scan dense data: use a list or table.
Grouping inside another card: use `l-stack` and a heading instead of a card in a card.
A page section with no border of its own: use `l-section`.
use: Place cards in l-grid or l-stack; the layout sets the gap between cards.
For c-card--interactive, make the card an <a> or put one link inside whose area covers the card.
avoid: Putting several competing links inside a c-card--interactive.

do.text: Put the link on the title and add c-card--interactive; the link covers the card and other actions stay clickable.

whenToUse: Any form control that needs a label, help text or an error message.

Help text explains format or why you ask; keep it to one sentence.
Mark optional fields "(optional)" and ask only for what you need.
After a failed submit, list every error at the top of the form, each linked to its field.

children: Order: c-form-field__label, then the control (c-input), then c-form-field__help and/or c-form-field__error.
a11y: Connect label and control with for/id.
Give help and error elements ids and list them in the control's aria-describedby.
Use role="alert" or a live region on the error when it appears after submit.

blocks.name: Input
blocks.description: Single-line text entry. Also styles <textarea> and <select>.

states.name: error
states.description: The value is invalid. Adds a heavier bottom edge so the state does not rely on color.
states.pair: Set aria-invalid="true" and aria-describedby pointing at the c-form-field__error message.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The field cannot be edited. Rendered ghosted with a dashed keyline.

whenToUse: One line of free text: a name, an email address, a search query, a number.
Multi-line text on a <textarea>, or a choice from many options on a <select>.
whenNotToUse: Choosing among 2 to 6 visible options: radio buttons read faster than a select (coming in 0.4.0).
A yes/no setting: a checkbox (coming in 0.4.0).
Showing a value that cannot change: plain text, not a read-only input.
use: Always wrap in c-form-field with a c-form-field__label.
Use the right type attribute (email, tel, number, search) so mobile keyboards match.
avoid: Using placeholder text as the only label.
Setting a width on .c-input; it fills its container. Constrain the container instead.

do.text: Give every input a visible label that stays visible while typing.

dont.text: Don't use the placeholder as the label: it disappears as soon as someone types.

do.text: Pair the error state with aria-invalid and link the message with aria-describedby.
do.html: Enter a start date after 1 January 2020.

dont.text: Don't show an error with a red border alone.

content: Error messages say what went wrong and how to fix it: "Enter a date after 1 January 2020", not "Invalid date".
Show errors when the person leaves the field or submits, not while they type the first value. Once a field is in error, clear the message as soon as it is fixed.
Mark the few optional fields with "(optional)" in the label; don't add asterisks to required ones.

a11y: Every input needs a programmatic label: <label for> on c-form-field__label.
Error text must be linked with aria-describedby, not only shown in red.

keyboard.action: Moves focus into and out of the field.

blocks.description: Deprecated standalone label. Use c-form-field__label inside c-form-field instead; c-label will be removed in 1.0.

whenToUse: Never in new code. Existing c-label markup keeps working until 1.0.
whenNotToUse: Labelling any form control: use `c-form-field` with c-form-field__label.

do.text: Use the form-field label.

dont.text: Don't use the deprecated block.

blocks.name: Modal
blocks.description: A dialog over the page that blocks interaction until dismissed. Works on <dialog> (preferred, opened with showModal()) or on a <div role="dialog">.

elements.name: backdrop
elements.description: Dimmed layer behind the dialog; clicking it may close the modal.

elements.name: header
elements.description: Holds the title and close button.

elements.name: close
elements.description: Icon button that closes the dialog.

elements.name: footer
elements.description: Actions, right-aligned. Put the primary action last.

states.name: closed
states.description: Hidden (div form). With <dialog>, use the open attribute / showModal() instead.
states.pair: When closed, return focus to the control that opened the modal.

whenToUse: Confirming a destructive or irreversible action, such as deleting a project.
A short task that must not lose the page behind it, such as renaming an item.
Warning that unsaved work will be lost.
whenNotToUse: Long or scrolling content, or anything with its own navigation: make it a page.
Success messages and tips: show them inline on the page.
Opening a dialog from a dialog: keep it to one level where you can, two at most.
use: Use for short, focused tasks: confirmations, small forms.
Buttons in c-modal__footer are c-button; the footer provides the gap. Use c-button--danger for destructive confirmations.
avoid: Opening a modal from another modal.
Long, scrolling content; use a page instead.

do.text: Use <dialog> opened with showModal(), named by its title, with verb buttons.
do.html: Discard your changes?

dont.text: Don't build a dialog from a bare <div>: no focus handling, no Escape, nothing announced.

do.text: Label the close button.
do.html: Share project

dont.text: Don't leave an icon-only close button without a name.
dont.html: Share project

content: Title the dialog with the question or task: "Delete this project?"
Button labels repeat the verb: "Delete project" and "Keep project", never "OK" and "Cancel".
Say what happens next in one or two sentences in the body.

children: c-modal contains c-modal__backdrop and c-modal__container as siblings.
c-modal__container contains header, body and footer in that order.
a11y: Prefer <dialog class="c-modal"> opened with showModal(): the browser then handles focus, Escape and inertness. With a <div>, set role="dialog", aria-modal="true" and manage focus yourself.
With the <div> form, make the page behind inert and lock scrolling while open, trap focus, close on Escape, and return focus to the opener.
c-modal__close needs aria-label="Close" and an SVG icon, not a text glyph.

keyboard.action: Closes the dialog and returns focus to the control that opened it.
Moves focus between controls inside the dialog only.

blocks.description: Single-purpose overrides with !important. Use sparingly; reach for a layout or component first.

classes.description: Align text to the start (left in left-to-right languages).

classes.description: Remove margin, e.g. from a heading or paragraph inside a component.

whenNotToUse: Spacing between components: use `l-stack` or `l-cluster`.
